hop.parent: the seat's live @pane_parent, which always wins; FLEET_PARENT is a launch-time cache, noted on stderr when unset or stale (hop.sh target exits 5 only when the live edge cannot be read or is malformed)
hop.chainFile: hop-chain.txt in the session directory, written by hop.sh chain at Setup
hop.carrier: an /ask file, per /ask — a new ask is written with Skill(ask, "<question> --to <parent> [--reserved-for operator]"); a pass-up moves an existing ask with engine ask forward <seat>/<id> --to <parent>, never a hand edit of to:; floor and reserved items carry reserved-for: operator
hop.rePing: manual — no timer (operator 23:05: push is fine; timers aren't). The seat's /next lists overdue asks; passing an ask further up is a deliberate step.

grant.version: v1 — the leans, decided by the operator 2026-10-28 23:13 (GRANTBOARD IDE-238; record builds/authority-grant_DECIDE.md). A living document: amendments go through RULINGS (IDE-233).
grant.amended: G and H delegated: the manager answers the /snapshot and /pr confirms and the wave-boundary merge confirm.

A.covers: assignment of an action the operator already approved
A.condition: the operator's approval can be found; the ruling picks or re-picks the performer only — never approves, enlarges or re-times the action
A.reversal: the approval cannot be found (then it is D or E), or the operator names a different performer

B.covers: a fast-forward or an append onto ground this fleet owns
B.condition: all four hold: (1) a fast-forward or an append, no rewrite of a pushed commit; (2) the branch was created by this weave or named as its ground; (3) no other seat holds a claim on it in the live registers; (4) the relevant gate ran green and the verdict was read, not the exit status
B.reversal: any one of the four fails — it is then class E

C.covers: a provisional working position for this weave only
C.condition: the ruling is written down as provisional, names the side picked and the escalation it stands in front of, keeps that escalation open, and flags the durable question in the hand-over
C.reversal: the weave boundary (it expires), or the operator's durable answer

D.covers: interpreting a ruling the operator already gave
D.condition: the instruction is clear in direction and silent on the detail; the reading is logged beside the words read
D.reversal: the reading widens the instruction, or the operator reads it otherwise

G.covers: the /snapshot and /pr confirms: a commit, a push of the work's own branch, a pull request, a ticket comment or status move (the operator does not confirm these one by one)
G.condition: the answer names the exact action (this commit, this PR, this comment); landing on a shared trunk still follows LANDING.md (the path owners' gos and the lease)
G.reversal: the action reaches another lead's project, production, or deletes data, or the answer names no exact action; then it is not G

H.covers: the wave-boundary merge confirm: approving the merge of a wave's verified work onto the session branch
H.condition: the wave's gate ran green and the verdict was read, not the exit status; the answer names the wave and the branch it merges onto
H.reversal: the gate is red or unread, or the merge lands on a shared trunk or outside ground this fleet owns; then it is not H
